definitions.name: Account Number

constraints.representation: Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Request: Format: 123456789012nn…nn Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric bytes) Account Number. Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Response: Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) Account Number. Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Request: Format: 123456789012nn…nn Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric bytes) Account Number. Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Response: Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) Account Number. TransArmor – All Messages: For all TransArmor formatting of the Account Number field, see Appendix AA. TransArmor Processing Considerations.

definitions.validCodesEvidence: Credit, debit, and EBT cards: Please refer to the most recent version of BUYPASS® Platform Issuer Identification Number (IIN) Reference Manual. Fleet cards: Please refer to the most recent version of BUYPASS® Platform Petroleum Industry Processing Specifications. Stored Value cards: The length of the Account Number should be 16 or 19 bytes. Note: For a First DataTM Premium Gift Card Transaction Response, the calculated card number is returned in the Account Number field.

definitions.validCodesEvidence: For a card whose number has been manually entered, the expiration date is in MMYY format, and the other required data depends upon the application. Note: For all authorizations, merchants must send a value even for expired cards. For a Certegy (Formerly Telecredit) transaction, the information consists of the 2-character alphabetical State Code (See Appendix D. Valid State Codes.) and the 6-character birth date (MMDDYY). If a driver's license number is used as identification for a SCAN (ETC) transaction, the information consists of the 2-character alphabetical State Code (See Appendix D. Valid State Codes.). For either TransArmor processing method, the expiration date must be included here. The expiration date is stored for follow-on transactions associated with a Token. For a Comdata Express Code or Check request (card type code 095/096), this field should be skipped. Field separators should be included as usual. For a Money Code/Check request (card type code 093), this field should be skipped. Field separators should be included as usual. For Accel and STAR: Expiration date is mandatory for e- commerce and one-time bill payment transactions. Effective May 1, 2025, expiration date is optional for Accel and STAR transactions, where the merchant retrieves the payment details from the merchant’s internal customer database to submit the transaction. These credentials on file (COF) transactions include bill payment, recurring, and installment payment transactions.

businessRules.title: Number of Card Types (Element 59) identifies how many times field 8 (Card Type) repeats — Card Type may repeat 01-99 times
A Card Type value of '173' in this segment's repeating Card Type field (Element 14) conditionally triggers Segment DL6 (Store and Forward) in the same Table Load Response

Each repeated Card Type (Element 14) must be a valid Appendix E 'Card Type Code Used in the Table Load Response': an accepted card type or a device feature code (for example 127, 148, 150, 162-168, 171, 173, 174); feature codes are never used in Prompt Codes
Segment DL6 is only sent in a Table Load Response when Segment DL1 (Merchant Data Segment) includes a Card Type value of 173 in Data Element No. 14 (Card Type)

Card Type 173 'Enables Store and Forward blocking for a designated range of time each day'; the DL6 Start Time and End Time define that daily recurring window during which the device blocks store-and-forward processing

businessRules.title: Element 63 equals serialized segment count
In a Totals Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) is 01
Segment 108 belongs exclusively to the Loyalty Card Transaction Request; it is not a Financial Transaction Request companion
In a Loyalty Card Transaction Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) counts Segment 100, Segment 108 and the optional Segment 114, so it is 2 or 3 and equals the number of segments present
Data Section 1 contains required Message Format Version Identifier (Element 55) and Number of Segments (Element 63), separated and followed by a Field Separator

An ECA/TeleCheck Service Transaction Request carries Segment 100, Segment 110 (Field No. 4) and Segment 111 (Field No. 5), plus the conditional Segment 113 (Field No. 6) and no other segment; Element 63 is therefore 3 or 4 and equals the number of segments present
Segment 113 belongs exclusively to the ECA/TeleCheck® Service Transaction Request; it is not a Financial Transaction Request companion
In a Totals with Proprietary Data Load Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) is 01, so Segment 119 is the only data segment

dependencies.title: Element 63 equals serialized segment count
In a Totals Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) is 01
Segment 105 is present in every Totals Request
Segment 108 belongs exclusively to the Loyalty Card Transaction Request; it is not a Financial Transaction Request companion
In a Loyalty Card Transaction Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) counts Segment 100, Segment 108 and the optional Segment 114, so it is 2 or 3 and equals the number of segments present
Data Section 1 contains required Message Format Version Identifier (Element 55) and Number of Segments (Element 63), separated and followed by a Field Separator

An ECA/TeleCheck Service Transaction Request carries Segment 100, Segment 110 (Field No. 4) and Segment 111 (Field No. 5), plus the conditional Segment 113 (Field No. 6) and no other segment; Element 63 is therefore 3 or 4 and equals the number of segments present
Segment 113 is a conditional member of the ECA/TeleCheck® Service Transaction Request's Data Section 3 (present when check-service risk-control data is being sent)

Segment 114 is exclusive to the Loyalty Card Transaction Request's Data Section 3; it is not documented as a companion in the Financial Transaction Request (11.1.1), ECA/TeleCheck Service Transaction Request (11.3.1), or CA Public Key File Load Request (11.9.1) Data Section 3 lists

Segment 116 (TransArmor Load Data Segment) is used for Key and Key ID Load in TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization processing; confirmed via the Element 63 (Number of Segments) and Element 85 (Segment Type) processing-rule text and valid-codes tables

The TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load Request contains Data Section 1 (Elements 55, 63) directly followed by Segment 116 in Field No. 3; by structural analogy with the sibling message types listed in the same Element 63 processing-rule paragraph (Totals, Loyalty Card, Electronic Mail, ECA/TeleCheck, Communications Test), the request likely excludes the Standard Message Data Segment (100) and carries no other segment, but this is not shown in a dedicated Segment 116 request table
In a Totals with Proprietary Data Load Request, Element 63 (Number of Segments) is 01, so Segment 119 is the only data segment
The EMV Financial Transaction Request Data Section 3 occupies Field Nos. 4-8 (five slots), so Segment 130 plus at most four companion segments may be present
In a CA Public Key File Load Request Segment 132 is in Field No. 3; whether Segments 101, 102, 104 and 111 may accompany it is unresolved

businessRules.title: Fuel products are always the first products in the segment
For EV charging transactions the EV product code is first
A unique Product Code is sent for each type of fuel purchase
Product Code is a valid value per Appendix F
Multi-fuel OTR transactions list the primary fuel first

When Prompt Code is 904 (Host Discount Data, response only), fields 14-27 are: Host Discount Timestamp (179, 12), Number of Discounts (171, 2), then a repeated block of Start Date (165,8), Start Time (166,4), End Date (165,8), End Time (166,4), BUYPASS Card Type (173,4), Card BIN Range Beginning (183,12), Card BIN Range Ending (184,12), Product Code (77,3), Product Discount Amount (172,5), Product Code (77,3), Discount Quantity Limit (185,3), Discount Program Description (186,15), for a total variable length not to exceed 3,600 bytes

The discount amount from Host Discount Data is carried in a subsequent Financial Transaction Request's Product Code Data Segment (102) using Product Code 941 (negative amount, post-pay environment) or 991 (administrative amount, pre-pay environment)

Tax by Product Data repeats per product for a maximum of 10 products, total variable length up to 360 bytes; each product entry contains Product Code (77) plus up to 3 tax sub-entries (Inclusive/Exclusive flag, Tax Type, Tax Amount)
Segment 157 does not allow any product codes above '899' except for '955' (Cash Back); if any other code above 899 is present, the transaction will be declined

Segment Type fixed 157, Segment Length 3 digits, Service Level (Element 87), Number of Products (Element 62, 2 digits), then per-product: Product Code (77, max 3 including 899-cap/955-exception), Unit of Measure (106), Quantity (81, 9 digits, must encode assumed decimal places as whole digits, e.g. 0.05 with 2 decimals = '205'), Unit Price (107, 9 digits, same decimal-encoding rule), Product Amount (76, 12 digits)

Prompt Code is 990
Prompt Code is required and must be 981 for standard retrieval, 996 for proprietary-card-data retrieval, or 995 for submission

Prompt Code (Element 78) is Required, field 6, 3 digits, and must be one of the five documented values: 901 (Custom receipt text), 902 (Dynamic card table), 903 (Site configuration data), 904 (Host discount data), 905 (Fuel volume data), per Appendix E's Valid Card Type Codes Used in Special Transaction Prompt Codes

Host Discount Data (Prompt Code 904) is triggered when a Totals Response's Response Code (83) indicates proprietary/host-discount data pending (values D/E for general proprietary data pending, M/N for Host Discount data pending specifically); the device then sends a Proprietary Data Load Request with Prompt Code 904
Prompt Code is fixed value 990

businessRules.title: Financial responses support approved purchase/capture response codes
Financial responses support approved authorization response codes
Partial approval responses carry an approved amount
Declined financial responses carry a decline code

Electronic Mail Response contains required Response Code, Download Indicator, Initiation Date, Initiation Time, Sequence Number, and Block Number; optional Mail Text Data Length and Mail Text Data are correlated

A Proprietary Data Load Response contains Data Section 1 (Response Code 83 pos.1 len.1, Download Indicator 30 pos.2 len.1, Initiation Date 45 pos.3 len.6, Initiation Time 46 pos.9 len.4, Sequence Number 86 pos.13 len.6, all Required) and Data Section 3 (field 6, Segment 118, Required)

Response Code (Element 83) values specific to the Proprietary Data Load context: H (Approved, proprietary data retrieval more pending), O (Approved, proprietary data load more pending), T (Approved, proprietary data load, no more data pending), U (Declined, proprietary data load, no more data pending), X (Declined, proprietary data load, proceed to next pending Prompt Code), Y (Approved, proprietary data load, proceed to next pending Prompt Code)

For Site Configuration Data (Prompt Code 903), Block Number starts at 1 and increments with each block; Block Number = 0 is sent as a final message and carries no site configuration data; the associated Response Codes are T (Approved, no more data pending) and U (Declined, no more data pending)

Host Discount Data (Prompt Code 904) is triggered when a Totals Response's Response Code (83) indicates proprietary/host-discount data pending (values D/E for general proprietary data pending, M/N for Host Discount data pending specifically); the device then sends a Proprietary Data Load Request with Prompt Code 904

Response Code (Element 83) values V (Declined, Totals with Proprietary Custom Receipt Text data pending) and W (Approved, Totals with Proprietary Custom Receipt Text pending) indicate that a Prompt Code 901 (Custom Receipt Text) load is pending, analogous to the Host Discount D/E/M/N pattern

Indicator length

businessRules.title: Additional Information (Element 118) is variable length and carries the value identified by its paired Indicator/Length
The EMV Additional Information Section (fields 7-9: Indicator, Length, Information) repeats per EMV Additional Information Indicator for a maximum total length of 2,000 bytes

Element 118 is reused across segments: it is 'Additional Information' in Segment 112 (max 984, single occurrence) and 'EMV Additional Information' in Segment 130 (variable length, repeating). Do not assume element numbers are globally unique or that the two fields share business meaning

Appendix T Table ID 001 (EMV Table Data) carries exactly EMVYES or EMVNOT, length 6, sent only in an EMV Transaction request; if returned in an authorization response the device echoes it on any subsequent advice or batch upload request
Appendix T Table ID 002 (Card Authentication Results Code, CARC) has Maximum Length 1 and carries the CARC value returned by Visa in Bit No. 44.8 of the response

The EMV Additional Information Section (fields 6-8: Indicator, Length, Information) repeats per EMV Additional Information Indicator for a maximum total length of 2,800 bytes — a DIFFERENT cap than Segment 130's 2,000-byte limit for the structurally identical section

Element 118 is reused across three segments now documented in this KB: Segment 112 ('Additional Information', single occurrence), Segment 130 ('EMV Additional Information', repeating, request-side), and Segment 131 ('EMV Additional Information', repeating, response-side)

definitions.name: Partial Approval Indicator

constraints.representation: Fixed length of 1 digit

definitions.validCodesEvidence: Value Description 0 Not specified (default)/Not supported This value is the default value. If the Merchant does not support credit/debit/fleet Partial Approvals, then this value is transmitted. 1 Supported This value indicates that the Merchant supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions. If the Merchant transmits this value with a transaction—and the corresponding network supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions—the network can approve an amount that is less than the amount in the Authorization request; and BUYPASS will send a Partial Approval response. The network may return a card balance that is printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 5 This value indicates that the Merchant only supports the receipt of the card balance, not Partial Approval transaction processing. The network may return a card balance that is printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. Note: This value is only supported for American Express prepaid cards. Note: Support for Partial Authorization is mandatory for all card brands. Data Element 121 ( Partial Approval Indicator) should be populated correctly for all card present transactions, showing that the terminal is capable of partial authorization responses. Note: For American Express transactions, Merchants sending transaction request amount as ‘zero’ and using values ‘1’ or ‘5’ for Prepaid card balances, will not be receiving the card balance back in response.

field.name: MICR Data
field.description: Identifies the check’s MICR data. Source: Device

businessRules.title: MICR Data (Element 122) is required, alphanumeric, maximum 50 bytes, and required on all check transactions; when raw MICR data exceeds 50 bytes, only the first 50 bytes (left to right) are placed here and the remainder is expected in Extended MICR Data (Element 137), whose hosting data segment is not confirmed by the extracted Segment 110 table

Two MICR encodings are documented in narrative text: Full MICR Line TAC format (example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999) and Full MICR Line RAW TOAD format (symbol substitution using T, O, A, D); Alternate MICR IND = 'Y' signals RAW TOAD/ALB1 format, but no machine-checkable grammar beyond the example and the 50-byte length limit is given

MICR Data (Element 122) is cross-referenced from Account Number (Element 2) of the Standard Message Data Segment (100); the extract states MICR data 'is also included' there but does not state a byte-identity or co-validation rule between the two representations

definitions.name: EMV Chip Data

constraints.representation: Variable length of 999 characters, preceded by three digit length indicator All fields after the table length are in binary format.

definitions.validCodesEvidence: The components of EMV data elements are described below: Component Name: Tag Each sub element or Tag can be either one or two bytes long. To determine the length, check the last five bits of the first byte, if they are all on (1) the tag of the sub element is two bytes long, including the current byte. Example 1: Tag x’9F10’ is a two byte tag - the last five bits of the first byte (x’9F’) are all ones. Example 2: Tag x’72’ is a one byte tag - the last five bits of the first byte (x’72’) are not all ones. Component Name: Length (ANSB …127) The next one or more bytes are the length indicator of the tag. To determine the number of length bytes used for this inspect the first byte of the length field. If the first bit of the first byte is a 1, the remaining bits (next seven) are a binary representation of the number of following bytes of the length field. If the first bit is 0, the remaining bits indicate the actual length of the data that follows. Example 1: If the length byte is x’0C’, then 12 is the length of the data that follows the sub element. Example 2: If the tag is x’82’, the length is contained in the next byte of the sub element. The value in the length byte indicates the number of bytes of data following.

definitions.name: Token Requestor ID

constraints.representation: Fixed length of 11 bytes

definitions.validCodesEvidence: Position Description 1-11 Token Requestor ID, Left justified, space-filled Note: In late 2014, MasterCard introduced the Card on File tokenization service and static card on file token type to support token payments for e-Commerce merchants that traditionally stored credit card numbers. MasterCard required merchants to submit the Token Requestor ID for Card on File tokenized transactions. Effective 8 June 2021, MasterCard renamed the Card on File token type to “Static Token” type. Also, they removed the requirement to submit the Token Requestor ID. However, if submitted, MasterCard will validate and will decline if invalid. Merchants are advised not to send the Token Requestor ID if submitting a Card on File tokenized transaction/Static Token type. Cryptographic Data is still not required for Static Tokens. Merchants that submit Secure Element and Cloud-based token types are still required to submit the Token Requestor ID along with Cryptographic data, if applicable.

This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction. In EMV transactions, if ‘S’ is returned in response, then subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must be sent as debit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction.

field.name: Alternate MICR IND
field.description: Denotes that the merchant supports the Alternate MICR format. This field is optional. Hence, this field is not required for merchants who do not support the Alternate MICR format. Value ‘Y’ - Indicates that the Alternate MICR format is being sent from the terminal. Fixed: 1 Byte Source: Device

businessRules.title: Alternate MICR IND, documented in Section 12.9 as Segment 110 field 12 using element number 239, is optional, fixed 1 byte, and its only documented value is 'Y' (Alternate/RAW TOAD MICR format is being sent); this element number is separately defined in the Chapter 13 master element catalog as 'Enhanced Fleet Data' (999 bytes, used by Segment 145). Per SME decision (2026-09-26), both usages are modeled as distinct, segment-scoped entities (element 239 @ Segment 110 vs. element 239 @ Segment 145); this rule intentionally remains REVIEW_REQUIRED by design, not due to a gap

Two MICR encodings are documented in narrative text: Full MICR Line TAC format (example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999) and Full MICR Line RAW TOAD format (symbol substitution using T, O, A, D); Alternate MICR IND = 'Y' signals RAW TOAD/ALB1 format, but no machine-checkable grammar beyond the example and the 50-byte length limit is given

Enhanced Fleet Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, containing one or more sub-segments in <tag><len><data> format, cataloged as: Table 001 (Request Flags, incl. Commercial/Retail Flag), Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Data, product-category-coded, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 004 (Prompt Data, authorizer-specific prompt tokens, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 006 (Money Code Payee Name), Table 007 (Money Code Check Number, required for all Money Code transactions), Table 008 (Cash Advance Limit)

Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Data) product categories are authorizer-specific; a documented list applies to WEX OTR transactions (e.g., ADD, ANFR, BRAK, ... WWFL); other authorizers' category lists are not enumerated in this section

Table 004 (Prompt Data) prompt tokens are authorizer-specific and independently cataloged for Voyager EMV (DF-tag-based), Visa Fleet 2.0, Comdata, WEX OTR, and Conexxus (numeric prompt codes, used by MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV); full enumeration of all prompt-token tables is out of scope for this rule catalog pass

Enhanced Fleet Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, cataloged as: Table 001 (Response Flags, incl. Settlement Indicator: CP/DB/DF/RC/RF/FN), Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Limits, NOT present in Comdata responses), Table 003 (Fuel Product Limits, using Appendix F product codes), Table 004 (Prompt Formats, using documented edit masks), Table 005 (Customer Information: name/city/state/account code), Table 010 (Additional Response Data: FNAM/LNAM/ATHN/ACCT/DMSG)

Table 004 (Prompt Formats) uses a documented edit-mask grammar: '?' (re-prompt), 'A'/'B' (alphanumeric, treated identically since 2015-01-02), 'N' (numeric only), 'I' (free format), 'O' (optional response), 'Z' (capture but don't resend), 'T' (data type N=Number/S=String), 'Mn'/'Xn' (min/max), 'Vn' (exact match), 'Pn' (pattern match using @ /# /* /literal)
Table 003 (Fuel Product Limits) uses standard product codes from ATL105 Appendix F (Valid Payment Systems Product Codes) — unlike Table 002's non-fuel category codes

Network Token Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, cataloged as 6 fixed sub-tables: 001 (Network Token, 013-018 bytes), 002 (Expiration Date, fixed 004), 003 (Provisional Fee Indicator, fixed 001), 004 (Input Indicator, fixed 001), 005 (Eligible Indicator, fixed 001), 006 (PAN Indicator, fixed 001)
